subject: General Test (Code: 501)

The last 5 questions are a data-interpretation set based on one table; the set stays together.

questions.sub_topic: Organs and the systems they belong to
questions.question:
Match the organs in List-I with the body systems in List-II:

List-I
(A) Heart
(B) Lungs
(C) Kidneys
(D) Brain

List-II
(I) Nervous system
(II) Excretory system
(III) Respiratory system
(IV) Circulatory system
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: Heart — circulatory system (IV); lungs — respiratory system (III); kidneys — excretory system (II); brain — nervous system (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps the heart and lungs; (C) swaps the lungs and kidneys; (D) swaps the kidneys and brain.
Key point: The lungs also help in excretion by removing carbon dioxide.

questions.sub_topic: Inequality chain with a reversed conclusion
questions.question:
Given that P < Q ≤ R, S > R and T ≤ P, decide which conclusions are definitely true.
Conclusions:
I. S > T
II. R > S
options: C) Both I and II follow
D) Neither I nor II follows
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Only I follows
Answer steps: combine the statements: S > R ≥ Q > P ≥ T. So S > T (I). The statement S > R directly contradicts R > S, so II does not follow.
Why not the others: (B) and (C) accept II, the reverse of a given statement. (D) rejects I, which follows from the chain.
Key point: Rewrite every statement so the signs point the same way, then read across.

questions.sub_topic: Mughal emperor who abolished the jizya
questions.question: Which Mughal emperor abolished the jizya, a tax on non-Muslims, in 1564?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Akbar
Why: Akbar abolished the jizya and the pilgrim tax as part of his policy of religious tolerance (sulh-i-kul).
Why not the others: (C) brought the jizya back in 1679. (A) and (D) ruled before the tax was abolished.
Key point: Akbar also started the Din-i-Ilahi and held debates at the Ibadat Khana in Fatehpur Sikri.

questions.sub_topic: Why clothes dry faster on a windy day
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Wet clothes dry faster on a windy day.
Reason (R): The wind lowers the temperature of the clothes.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
Why: (A) is true, but (R) is not the reason: wind carries away the moist air around the clothes, so more water can evaporate. Lowering the temperature would slow evaporation, not speed it up.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) accept the Reason as given. (D) calls the true Assertion false.
Key point: Evaporation is faster with more wind, higher temperature, larger surface area and lower humidity.

questions.sub_topic: City called the Pink City
questions.question: Which Indian city is known as the "Pink City"?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Jaipur
Why: The old city of Jaipur was painted pink (terracotta) in 1876 to welcome the Prince of Wales. The Walled City of Jaipur is a World Heritage Site.
Why not the others: (A) is the "Blue City". (C) is the "City of Lakes". (D) is the "Golden City".
Key point: Jaipur was founded by Sawai Jai Singh II in 1727.

questions.sub_topic: Assertion and reason on squares of odd numbers
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The square of every odd number is odd.
Reason (R): The product of two odd numbers is always odd.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Answer steps: both are true. Squaring an odd number multiplies it by itself, an odd number, so by (R) the result is odd. (R) explains (A).
Why not the others: (B) denies the link. (C) and (D) call a true statement false.
Key point: odd × odd = odd; any number × even = even.

questions.sub_topic: Mirror used by dentists
questions.question: Which kind of mirror do dentists use to see enlarged images of teeth?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Concave mirror
Why: An object placed close to a concave mirror (within its focus) forms an enlarged, upright image, so dentists see the teeth more clearly.
Why not the others: (B) always forms smaller images and is used to see a wide area. (C) forms images of the same size. (D) is not used for this.
Key point: Concave mirrors are also used in torches and car headlights.

questions.sub_topic: Statements about India's monsoon rainfall
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about rainfall in India:
A. The south-west monsoon brings most of India's rain between June and September.
B. Tamil Nadu gets much of its rain from the north-east (retreating) monsoon.
C. Mawsynram in Meghalaya is one of the wettest places on Earth.
D. Monsoon rain is spread evenly through the year.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: B) A, B and C only
C) B, C and D only
D) A, B, C and D
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) A, B and C only
Why: A, B and C are correct: the Coromandel coast lies in the rain shadow of the south-west winds and receives its main rain in October–December.
Why not the others: D is wrong: most rain falls in four months, and the rest of the year is largely dry. Options (C) and (D) include D; (A) leaves out the correct statement C.
Key point: The monsoon usually reaches Kerala around 1 June.

questions.sub_topic: Winner of the 2026 Women's T20 World Cup
questions.question: Which team won the ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2026, beating England in the final at Lord's?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Australia
Why: Australia beat hosts England by seven wickets in the final at Lord's in July 2026, winning the title for a record seventh time.
Why not the others: (C) lost to England in a semi-final. (A) and (B) did not reach the final.
Key point: New Zealand won the previous Women's T20 World Cup, in 2024.

questions.sub_topic: Smallest four-digit multiple of 18
questions.question: What is the smallest four-digit number that is exactly divisible by 18?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 1008
Given: 1,000 ÷ 18 = 55 remainder 10.
Step 1: The next multiple is 18 × 56.
Step 2: = 1,008.
Common mistake: picking 1002, which is divisible by 6 but not by 9 (its digits add to 3), so not by 18.

questions.sub_topic: National aquatic animal of India
questions.question: What is the national aquatic animal of India?
options: B) Dugong (sea cow) of the Gulf of Mannar
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Ganges river dolphin
Why: The Ganges river dolphin was declared the national aquatic animal in 2009. It is almost blind and finds its way by echolocation; it lives in the Ganga–Brahmaputra river system.
Why not the others: (A) is an ocean mammal. (B) is an endangered sea mammal but not the national aquatic animal. (C) nests in large numbers on the Odisha coast.
Key point: The Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary is in Bihar.

questions.sub_topic: Counting a digit between two others
questions.question: In the sequence 3 7 5 2 3 7 8 3 7 5 7 5 3 7 5, how many times is 7 immediately preceded by 3 and immediately followed by 5?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 3
Answer steps: the groups "3 7 5" appear at positions 1–3, 8–10 and 13–15. The "3 7 8" group fails the second condition, and the 7 at position 11 follows a 5. So the answer is 3.
Why not the others: (A) misses one group. (B) counts every 7 that comes after a 3, including "3 7 8". (D) counts every 7 in the sequence.
Key point: Check both conditions for each 7 in turn.

questions.sub_topic: Who administers the President's oath
questions.question: Who administers the oath of office to the President of India?
options: D) Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Chief Justice of India
Why: Under Article 60, the oath is administered by the Chief Justice of India or, in his absence, by the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court.
Why not the others: (B) and (C) are themselves sworn in by the President. (D) presides over the Lok Sabha and has no role in the President's oath.
Key point: The President in turn administers the oath to the Vice-President and the Prime Minister.

questions.sub_topic: Gas given off when acid meets marble
questions.question: Which gas is given off when dilute hydrochloric acid is added to marble chips (calcium carbonate)?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Carbon dioxide
Why: Acids react with carbonates to give a salt, water and carbon dioxide: CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂. The gas turns lime water milky.
Why not the others: (B) is given off when acids react with metals. (C) is not produced. (D) is the gas that forms hydrochloric acid, not a product.
Key point: The lime-water test identifies carbon dioxide.

questions.sub_topic: Conclusions from a rule on water bottles
questions.question:
Statement: The school has made it compulsory for students to carry water bottles during the summer months.
Conclusions:
I. Students may suffer from dehydration in summer.
II. Students do not drink water at home.
options: B) Neither I nor II follows
D) Both I and II follow
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Only I follows
Answer steps: the rule is meant to keep students drinking water in the heat, so the school expects a risk of dehydration (I). Nothing in the statement is about drinking at home, so II does not follow.
Why not the others: (A) and (D) accept II, which is not linked to the rule. (B) rejects I, the reason for the rule.
Key point: A conclusion should explain the statement without adding new claims.

questions.sub_topic: Statements about the 2026 Commonwealth Games
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the 2026 Commonwealth Games:
A. They were held in Glasgow, Scotland.
B. They were held from 23 July to 2 August 2026.
C. India finished fourth on the medal table.
D. It was the first time Glasgow had hosted the Commonwealth Games.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: B) B, C and D only
C) A, B, C and D
D) A, B and C only
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) A, B and C only
Why: A, B and C are correct: India won 39 medals, including 13 gold, behind Australia, England and Canada.
Why not the others: D is wrong: Glasgow had also hosted the 2014 Commonwealth Games. Options (B) and (C) include D; (A) leaves out the correct statement C.
Key point: The 2030 Commonwealth Games are to be held in Ahmedabad.

questions.sub_topic: Statements about respiration and photosynthesis in plants
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about plants:
A. Plants respire both by day and by night.
B. Photosynthesis takes place only in the presence of light.
C. Plants release carbon dioxide during respiration.
D. Roots do not respire.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: B) A, B and C only
C) B, C and D only
D) A, B, C and D
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) A, B and C only
Why: A, B and C are correct: respiration goes on in every living cell at all times, while photosynthesis needs light.
Why not the others: D is wrong: root cells respire too, taking oxygen from air spaces in the soil — which is why waterlogged plants can die. Options (C) and (D) include D; (A) leaves out the correct statement C.
Key point: By day, photosynthesis is faster than respiration, so plants give out more oxygen than they use.

questions.sub_topic: Mountain peaks in order of height
questions.question:
Arrange the following peaks in order of height (highest first):
A. Nanda Devi
B. Anamudi
C. K2
D. Kangchenjunga
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) C, D, A, B
Why: K2 (8,611 m), Kangchenjunga (8,586 m), Nanda Devi (7,816 m), Anamudi (2,695 m).
Why not the others: (A) puts Kangchenjunga above K2. (B) puts Nanda Devi above Kangchenjunga. (D) puts Anamudi above Nanda Devi.
Key point: Anamudi, in Kerala, is the highest peak of peninsular India.

questions.sub_topic: International bodies and their reports
questions.question:
Match the organisations in List-I with the reports or indices they publish in List-II:

List-I
(A) UNDP
(B) World Economic Forum
(C) International Monetary Fund
(D) Transparency International

List-II
(I) Corruption Perceptions Index
(II) World Economic Outlook
(III) Global Gender Gap Report
(IV) Human Development Report
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: UNDP — Human Development Report, which includes the Human Development Index (IV); World Economic Forum — Global Gender Gap Report (III); IMF — World Economic Outlook (II); Transparency International — Corruption Perceptions Index (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps UNDP and the WEF; (B) swaps the WEF and the IMF; (D) swaps the IMF and Transparency International.
Key point: The Human Development Index combines life expectancy, education and income.

questions.sub_topic: What the 2026 Physics Nobel winner's observatory detects
questions.question: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded to Francis Halzen, who led the IceCube Observatory buried in the ice at the South Pole. IceCube detects:
options: A) gravitational waves from colliding black holes
D) radio signals from black holes
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) high-energy neutrinos from space
Why: IceCube uses sensors in a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice to catch rare flashes made by neutrinos — tiny, almost massless particles — arriving from distant cosmic sources. Halzen received the whole prize alone.
Why not the others: (A) are detected by laser instruments such as LIGO. (C) has not been directly detected. (D) are studied with radio telescopes.
Key point: Neutrinos pass through most matter without stopping, so huge detectors are needed.

questions.sub_topic: Niece through a father's daughter-in-law
questions.question: Pointing to a girl, Meera said, "She is the daughter of the only daughter-in-law of my father." How is the girl related to Meera?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Niece
Answer steps: Meera's father's only daughter-in-law is the wife of Meera's brother. The girl is that couple's daughter — Meera's brother's daughter, her niece.
Why not the others: (B) would need Meera to be the daughter-in-law, but she is the father's daughter. (C) would be a child of Meera's parents. (D) would be a child of Meera's uncle or aunt.
Key point: A father's daughter-in-law is a brother's wife.

questions.sub_topic: Time together when one is more efficient
questions.question: A is 50% more efficient than B. B alone can finish a job in 30 days. In how many days can A and B finish it together?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 12 days
Given: A does 1.5 times as much work per day as B, so A alone takes 30 ÷ 1.5 = 20 days.
Step 1: Together per day = 1/20 + 1/30 = 5/60 = 1/12.
Step 2: Together they take 12 days.
Common mistake: taking "50% more efficient" to mean A needs half the time (15 days, option A), or averaging the two times (25 days, option D).

questions.sub_topic: Instrument for body temperature
questions.question: Which instrument is used to measure the temperature of the human body?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Thermometer
Why: A clinical thermometer measures body temperature; normal body temperature is about 37 °C (98.6 °F).
Why not the others: (A) measures air pressure. (B) measures humidity. (D) measures blood pressure.
Key point: A clinical thermometer usually reads from 35 °C to 42 °C.

questions.sub_topic: Average of the first twenty odd numbers
questions.question: What is the average of the first 20 odd numbers (1, 3, 5, …, 39)?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 20
Given: the sum of the first n odd numbers is n².
Step 1: Sum = 20² = 400.
Step 2: Average = 400 ÷ 20 = 20.
Common mistake: giving the last odd number (39, option D), or taking the 21st odd number's position (21, option A).

questions.sub_topic: Change in area when the radius grows
questions.question: The radius of a circle is increased by 50%. By what percentage does its area increase?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 125%
Given: area is proportional to the square of the radius.
Step 1: New radius = 1.5r, so new area = 2.25 × old area.
Step 2: Increase = 2.25 − 1 = 1.25, that is 125%.
Common mistake: assuming the area grows by the same 50% (option B), or giving the new area as a percentage of the old (225%, option D).

questions.sub_topic: Number from the gap with its square root
questions.question: A number exceeds its own square root by 12. What is the number?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 16
Given: let √x = y, so x = y² and y² − y = 12.
Step 1: y² − y − 12 = 0, so (y − 4)(y + 3) = 0, and y = 4 (a square root here is positive).
Step 2: x = 16. (Check: 16 − 4 = 12.)
Common mistake: testing only one option — 9 − 3 = 6, 25 − 5 = 20 and 36 − 6 = 30 do not give 12.

questions.sub_topic: Simple interest for a period with a half-year
questions.question: What is the simple interest on ₹4,000 at 12% per annum for 2½ years?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) ₹1,200
Given: P = ₹4,000; R = 12%; T = 2.5 years.
Step 1: SI = 4,000 × 12 × 2.5 ÷ 100.
Step 2: = ₹1,200.
Common mistake: leaving out the half-year (₹960, option A), or rounding up to 3 years (₹1,440, option C).

questions.sub_topic: Letter series in steps of three
questions.question: Which letter continues the pattern B, E, H, K, N …?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Q
Answer steps: each letter is three places after the one before: B (2), E (5), H (8), K (11), N (14), so the next is 17 — Q.
Why not the others: (A) moves two places. (C) moves four places. (D) moves one place.
Key point: Write the alphabet positions to check the step.

questions.sub_topic: Professions of five people
questions.question: P, Q, R, S and T are a doctor, an engineer, a lawyer, a teacher and a pilot, one each. R is the lawyer. P is the pilot. Q is neither the doctor nor the engineer. S is not the engineer. Who is the engineer?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) T
Answer steps: R is the lawyer and P the pilot, leaving doctor, engineer and teacher for Q, S and T. Q is not the doctor or the engineer, so Q is the teacher. S is not the engineer, so S is the doctor. T is the engineer.
Why not the others: (A) Q is the teacher. (B) S is the doctor. (C) R is the lawyer.
Key point: Fill in the certain facts first and eliminate step by step.

questions.sub_topic: Date of the fourth Saturday of a month
questions.question: In a certain month, the 3rd is a Monday. On which date does the fourth Saturday of that month fall?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 22
Answer steps: if the 3rd is a Monday, the 2nd is a Sunday and the 1st is a Saturday. The Saturdays are the 1st, 8th, 15th and 22nd, so the fourth Saturday is the 22nd.
Why not the others: (A) takes the first Saturday as the 8th, missing the 1st. (C) and (D) are not Saturdays (they are a Tuesday and a Wednesday).
Key point: Count back to the 1st of the month before counting forward.

questions.sub_topic: Syllogism of cars, buses and trucks
questions.question:
Statements:
Some cars are buses.
No bus is a truck.
Conclusions:
I. Some cars are not trucks.
II. Some trucks are cars.
options: C) Both I and II follow
D) Neither I nor II follows
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Only I follows
Answer steps: the cars that are buses cannot be trucks, so some cars are not trucks (I). Whether any truck is a car is not known, so II does not follow.
Why not the others: (A) and (C) accept II, which is only possible. (D) rejects I, which follows.
Key point: "Some A are B" with "No B is C" gives "Some A are not C".

questions.sub_topic: Cost price from the gap between loss and gain
questions.question: An article is sold at a loss of 10%. If it had been sold for ₹60 more, there would have been a gain of 5%. What is its cost price?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) ₹400
Given: going from a 10% loss to a 5% gain is a change of 15% of the cost price.
Step 1: 15% of CP = ₹60.
Step 2: CP = 60 ÷ 0.15 = ₹400.
Common mistake: treating ₹60 as 10% of the cost (₹600, option A) or as 5% (₹1,200, option B).

questions.sub_topic: Relationship among women, mothers and doctors
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes how the classes "Women", "Mothers" and "Doctors" are related?
options: A) Every woman is a mother, and no doctor is a mother.
B) Mothers, women and doctors are three separate groups with nothing in common.
C) All mothers are women; some women and some mothers may be doctors.
D) All doctors are mothers, and all mothers are women.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) All mothers are women; some women and some mothers may be doctors.
Answer steps: every mother is a woman, so the mothers lie inside the women. Some women — including some mothers — are doctors, and some doctors are men, so the doctors overlap both groups.
Why not the others: (A) wrongly makes every woman a mother and keeps mothers out of medicine. (B) ignores that every mother is a woman. (D) wrongly makes every doctor a mother.
Key point: In a Venn diagram, a class wholly inside another is drawn as a circle within a circle.

questions.sub_topic: Percentage who failed in both subjects
questions.question: In an examination, 60% of the students passed in English, 70% passed in Mathematics and 40% passed in both. What percentage of the students failed in both subjects?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 10%
Given: passed in at least one subject = 60 + 70 − 40.
Step 1: = 90%.
Step 2: Failed in both = 100 − 90 = 10%.
Common mistake: subtracting 40% from 70% (30%, option A), or adding 60% and 70% without removing the overlap and getting more than 100%.

questions.sub_topic: Host country of COP31
questions.question: COP31, the UN climate conference of November 2026, is held at Antalya. Which country hosts it, with Australia leading the negotiations?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Türkiye
Why: Under a deal reached at COP30, Türkiye hosts COP31 at Antalya and holds its presidency, while Australia acts as "President of Negotiations".
Why not the others: (A) hosted COP27 (2022). (B) hosted COP30 at Belém (2025). (D) hosted COP29 at Baku (2024).
Key point: COP stands for the Conference of the Parties to the UN climate convention (UNFCCC).

questions.sub_topic: Animals and their young
questions.question: Cow : Calf :: Dog : ?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Puppy
Answer steps: a calf is the young of a cow; a puppy is the young of a dog.
Why not the others: (A) is the young of a cat. (B) is the young of a lion, tiger or bear. (C) is the young of a horse.
Key point: The young of a goat is a kid, and of a sheep a lamb.

questions.sub_topic: Planets in order of distance from the Sun
questions.question:
Arrange the following planets in order of their distance from the Sun (nearest first):
A. Mars
B. Earth
C. Jupiter
D. Venus
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) D, B, A, C
Why: Venus (2nd), Earth (3rd), Mars (4th), Jupiter (5th).
Why not the others: (A) puts Earth before Venus. (B) puts Mars before Earth. (D) puts Jupiter before Mars.
Key point: The asteroid belt lies between Mars and Jupiter.

questions.sub_topic: Train speed from crossing two platforms
questions.question: A train crosses a platform 120 m long in 15 seconds and another platform 240 m long in 21 seconds. What is the speed of the train?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 72 km/h
Given: the extra 120 m of platform takes 21 − 15 = 6 extra seconds.
Step 1: Speed = 120 ÷ 6 = 20 m/s.
Step 2: In km/h: 20 × 18/5 = 72 km/h. (The train is 20 × 15 − 120 = 180 m long.)
Common mistake: giving the speed in m/s without converting (20, option B).

questions.sub_topic: Organisations of the freedom struggle and their founders
questions.question:
Match the organisations in List-I with the leaders linked to their founding in List-II:

List-I
(A) Forward Bloc
(B) Ghadar Party
(C) Home Rule League (1916)
(D) Hindustan Socialist Republican Association

List-II
(I) Bhagat Singh and Chandrashekhar Azad
(II) Annie Besant
(III) Lala Har Dayal
(IV) Subhas Chandra Bose
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: Forward Bloc — Subhas Chandra Bose, 1939 (IV); Ghadar Party — Lala Har Dayal and others, in San Francisco, 1913 (III); Home Rule League — Annie Besant, at Madras, 1916, alongside Tilak's league at Poona (II); HSRA — Bhagat Singh, Chandrashekhar Azad and others, 1928 (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps the Forward Bloc and Ghadar Party; (B) swaps the Ghadar Party and Home Rule League; (C) swaps the Home Rule League and HSRA.
Key point: The Ghadar Party was formed by Indians living in North America.

questions.sub_topic: Slope of a line through two points
questions.question: What is the slope of the line passing through the points (2, 3) and (6, 11)?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 2
Given: slope = (y₂ − y₁) ÷ (x₂ − x₁).
Step 1: = (11 − 3) ÷ (6 − 2) = 8 ÷ 4.
Step 2: = 2.
Common mistake: dividing the change in x by the change in y (4 ÷ 8 = ½, option B).

questions.sub_topic: Country of the 2026 Literature Nobel winner
questions.question: Anne Carson, awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in October 2026, is a poet and essayist from which country?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Canada
Why: Anne Carson is a Canadian poet and classical scholar known for works that mix poetry, essay and translation of ancient Greek texts. The award was announced on 8 October 2026.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) are other English-speaking countries.
Key point: Alice Munro (2013) was the first Canadian writer to win the Literature Nobel.

questions.sub_topic: State that protects the Indian wild ass
questions.question: The Indian wild ass is protected mainly in a sanctuary in the Little Rann of Kutch. In which state is it?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Gujarat
Why: The Wild Ass Sanctuary in the Little Rann of Kutch, Gujarat, set up in 1972, is the last home of the Indian wild ass (ghudkhur).
Why not the others: (A) has the Desert National Park, home of the great Indian bustard. (B) and (C) do not have wild ass habitats.
Key point: The Rann is a vast salt marsh that floods in the monsoon.

questions.sub_topic: Coding that changes only the vowels
questions.question: In a certain code, EDUCATION is written as FDVCBTJPN: each vowel is replaced by the next letter of the alphabet, and the consonants stay the same. How is HOUSE written in that code?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) HPVSF
Answer steps: H stays H; O → P; U → V; S stays S; E → F. HOUSE → HPVSF.
Why not the others: (A) changes the consonants too. (B) leaves U unchanged. (C) leaves O unchanged.
Key point: Check which letters the rule changes and which it leaves alone.

questions.sub_topic: Day of a meeting from two remarks
questions.question: Ravi remembers that a meeting is after Wednesday but before Saturday. Sita remembers that it is after Thursday. Both are right. On which day is the meeting?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Friday
Answer steps: Ravi's remark allows Thursday or Friday. Sita's remark rules out Thursday. So the meeting is on Friday.
Why not the others: (B) is ruled out by Sita. (C) is ruled out by Ravi ("before Saturday"). (D) is ruled out by both.
Key point: List the days each remark allows and take the common one.

questions.sub_topic: Hardest natural substance
questions.question: Which is the hardest naturally occurring substance?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Diamond
Why: Diamond, a form of carbon in which each atom is strongly bonded to four others, is the hardest natural material. It is used to cut glass and drill rock.
Why not the others: (A) is a fairly soft metal. (B) is hard but much softer than diamond. (C) is a very hard metal but still softer than diamond.
Key point: Diamond and graphite are both carbon, but graphite is soft and slippery.

Question: In which state did tourist arrivals fall from 2024 to 2025?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Sikkim
Given: 2025 figures compared with 2024: Kerala 207 > 180, Goa 88 > 80, Rajasthan 165 > 150, Uttarakhand 132 > 120, Sikkim 95 < 100.
Step 1: Only one state has a smaller figure in 2025.
Step 2: That state is Sikkim.
Common mistake: picking the state with the fewest arrivals (Goa, option A), which still rose.

questions.question:

Question: By what percentage did tourist arrivals in Kerala rise from 2024 to 2025?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 15%
Given: Kerala 180 lakh (2024), 207 lakh (2025).
Step 1: Increase = 27 lakh.
Step 2: Percentage rise = 27 ÷ 180 × 100 = 15%.
Common mistake: giving the rise in lakh as a percentage (27%, option B), or dividing by the 2025 figure (27 ÷ 207 ≈ 13%, option C).

Question: By how many lakh must tourist arrivals in Sikkim rise in 2026, compared with 2025, so that they are 20% higher than in 2024?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 25 lakh
Given: Sikkim 100 lakh (2024), 95 lakh (2025).
Step 1: Target = 100 × 1.2 = 120 lakh.
Step 2: Rise needed = 120 − 95 = 25 lakh.
Common mistake: measuring from 2024 instead of 2025 (20 lakh, option B), or taking 20% of the 2025 figure (19 lakh, option C).
